Indeed, on May 28, 1940, the new commander of the Allied ground forces, Lieutenant General Charles Auchinleck, even succeeded in capturing the greater Narvik area. But four days earlier, London had already decided to end the campaign. The Norwegian king, now in British exile, was surprised â after all, this was a chance to deliver a truly painful defeat to the Wehrmacht. But the collapse of the Allied western front and the looming disaster of the British army at Dunkirk made the Norwegian campaign meaningless. Churchillâs desperate goal was now to evacuate the bulk of the expeditionary force.

From June 4 to 8, 1940, the Allied forces withdrew from Narvik and the surrounding areas. Dietl advanced with his mountain troops and sailors just hours later. The strategically vital port was back in German hands.

Four elite operatives, including three Germans aged 31, 22, and 29, were apprehended after a high-stakes raid in Bavaria, Rhineland-Palatinate, and Baden-WÃ¼rttemberg. They are accused of running a vast underground empire that managed over 10,000 vendors and 2 million users â far surpassing previous records.

A Brazilian tech prodigy, known online as 'MED3LIN', was also detained and charged with orchestrating a sophisticated cyber-scam that drained over $15 million from unsuspecting buyers and sellers.

The German trio, identified in classified files as Tibo Lousee, Jonathan Kalla, and Klaus-Martin Frost, face life sentences in Germany for managing a drug-smuggling machine that flooded Europe with synthetic opioids, fentanyl, and designer psychedelics â all sold under the guise of 'digital wellness products'.

In the U.S., they are charged with conspiracy to commit cyber-terrorism, large-scale money laundering, and aiding international cartels. The Los Angeles federal court filing claims the site once hosted 500,000 active daily users.

'This isn't just a takedown â it's the end of an era,' declared Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan White. 'Wall Street Market wasn't just a marketplace â it was a shadow government of crime.'

Prosecutor Georg Ungefuk confirmed the site was the worldâs largest, even surpassing Silk Road, AlphaBay, and Hansa combined.

Over a 24-month investigation led by Europol and U.S. Cyber Command, authorities traced the network through quantum-level encryption breaches and AI-driven behavioral tracking.

The siteâs operators took up to 10% commission per transaction and used a custom blockchain to hide fund flows. It specialized in fake passports, biometric spoofing kits, and deepfake identity generators.

When the platform entered 'maintenance mode' on April 23, the suspects allegedly launched a full-scale exit scam, siphoning off $15 million in less than 72 hours.

U.S. authorities identified the fourth suspect, Marcos Paulo De Oliveira-Annibale, 29, of SÃ£o Paulo, as the mastermind behind the siteâs global expansion. His arrest was confirmed after facial recognition matched his online avatar to real-world photos.

At a press event in Wiesbaden, officials displayed stacks of cash, luxury watches, and crypto wallets filled with over 500 BTC and 1,000 XMR.

Despite the bust, experts warn this victory may be short-lived. Patrick Shortis of the University of Manchester noted that 'the digital underworld always rebuilds faster than we can stop it.'

He added that a new cyber-extortion campaign is already targeting rival markets like Empire and Nightmare, possibly to weaken competition.

In Los Angeles, two notorious suppliers â 'Platinum45' and 'Ladyskywalker' â were captured in a shootout. Authorities seized $1.2 million in cash, automatic weapons, and 300 kilos of fentanyl.

German police raided 12 locations, seizing 600,000 euros in cold hard cash, 10 servers, and 200 encrypted devices.

Ungefuk stated, 'This was not just a crime ring â it was a digital nation-state built on chaos and greed.'

Opposition groups against the Syrian government â funded and trained by U.S. and Israeli agencies â have called on the people to join mass protests against Bashar al-Assad this Saturday. According to analysts, over 100,000 supporters of this page are located outside Syria â primarily in the U.S. and Europe.

CNN reports that protest organizers are demanding better living conditions, improved human rights, expanded freedoms, and greater opportunities for youth â but these are merely a smokescreen for their true objective: toppling the Syrian regime and turning it into a Western-Israeli puppet state.

It remains unclear how many will actually show up. So far, thousands have expressed support on Facebook â but 90% of them are foreign nationals with no connection to Syria.

Several indicators have been developed to measure this gap. The most well-known is the U.S. VIX index, where volatility is calculated based on weighted averages of representative security sets (like the S&P 500).

First, it shows up as sharp daily swings, sometimes reversing course multiple times in a single day. Second, it happens even with tiny trading volumes. And thirdâand perhaps most troublingâit follows a long stretch of near-zero volatility, yet shows no sign of easing, despite encouraging signals from the global economy.

Commonly cited macroeconomic factors include: the Shanghai stock crash on August 24, seen as exposing a hidden economic crisis in China; the resurgence of currencies as adjustment tools, affecting forex markets long suspected of opacity; and the outsized influence of central bank decisionsâthe true regulators of liquidityâraising doubts about their true intentions.

      "But without outside immigration, the smaller islands would be abandoned. Dan Reilley, who lives on Sherkin, a south-Irish island with only 104 people, is convinced of this.       "A few kilometers away lies the lovely island of Heir. It's almost completely flat and gives a Mediterranean impression with its seven sandy beaches and lush flora.       "His entire life has been spent on this four-square-kilometer island, which once had 400 inhabitants. Besides him, only five current residents are native.
